raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "0.8.2"

package:
  name: python-hyperscan
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/h/hyperscan/hyperscan-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 1724e87e8f77f033a4592dc2cda7aecd10c91dfc718b55fa5379d0c95cff28e8

build:
  number: 0
  skip: win
  # Left to itself the upstream CMakeLists.txt downloads Boost, PCRE and
  # vectorscan and builds them in-tree, which cannot work without network
  # access. Setting both HS_SRC_ROOT and HS_BUILD_LIB_ROOT selects upstream's
  # "pre-built Hyperscan" path, which links the static libhs/libhs_runtime/
  # libchimera/libpcre already in the host prefix instead.
  script:
    # rattler-build exports CMAKE_GENERATOR="Unix Makefiles". Because that is
    # set rather than unset, scikit-build-core skips both its Ninja default and
    # its make fallback, and the build environment ships no make.
    - export CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja
    - >
      ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
      --config-settings=cmake.define.HS_SRC_ROOT=$PREFIX/include/hs
      --config-settings=cmake.define.HS_BUILD_LIB_ROOT=$PREFIX/lib

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - cmake
    - ninja
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then:
        - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
        - python
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    - scikit-build-core
    - vectorscan
    # libpcre.a is linked directly into the extension alongside libchimera.a
    - pcre
  run:
    - python
  ignore_run_exports:
    by_name:
      # vectorscan and pcre are consumed as static archives, so nothing is
      # left to link against at runtime.
      - pcre

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - hyperscan
      pip_check: true
  # vectorscan, chimera and PCRE are linked in as static archives, so a broken
  # chimera or a PCRE built without Unicode support would still import cleanly.
  # The upstream suite covers both.
  - script:
      - pytest -v tests/
    requirements:
      run:
        - pytest
        - pytest-mock
    files:
      source:
        - tests/

about:
  summary: Python bindings for Hyperscan.
  description: |
    A CPython extension for Vectorscan, an open source fork of Hyperscan,
    Intel's open source (prior to version 5.4), high-performance multiple
    regex matching library.
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  homepage: https://github.com/darvid/python-hyperscan
  documentation: https://python-hyperscan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - chrisburr
